run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The cart service is down: the only cart pod (cart-74587775fc-f2gwb) is in CrashLoopBackOff, exiting with code 139 after throwing 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' from cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected/Initialize, so the cart Deployment reports no available/ready replicas and the cart Service has only a not-ready endpoint. The pod that ran before it (cart-74587775fc-zmjv9, same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc and therefore same pod template) logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 06:56:30 and served GetCart/AddItem/EmptyCart until 06:57:23, then was stopped at 06:57:25 and replaced. The valkey-cart server itself is up, ready and restart-free with plenty of memory, endpoints populated, but its INFO errorstats show errorstat_NOAUTH rising from 1626 (06:58:25) to 2096 (06:59:38) with total_error_replies 1628->2098: it is now rejecting unauthenticated client commands with NOAUTH, while the cart container declares no Redis credentials (deployment cart env only has VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379). The valkey server runs with an empty config_file and its Deployment (generation 1, helm apply 06:56:24) declares no command/args/env, so the authentication requirement is not declared in the workload spec; the requirepass parameter is present but its value is redacted and could not be read. Consequence, each with its own error spans: checkout fails at oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (grpc 14, 'connect: connection refused' to 10.96.101.179:8080) and returns INTERNAL 13 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'; frontend fails POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout with HTTP 500; frontend-proxy and load-generator show 500s in the same traces. Brief startup-time ECONNREFUSED errors to product-catalog (10.96.4.197:8080) and flagd (10.96.137.224:8013) at 06:56:50-06:57:03 were considered and are not tied to this cause. Conclusion is partial: the auth requirement on the valkey-cart server is the supported cause of the cart crashloop, but its value and the exact time it was applied are not observable, and the actor that stopped the old cart pod is unknown.

claims.text: Pod cart-74587775fc-f2gwb (created 2026-11-25T06:57:25Z by ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc) has its cart container in state terminated with exitCode 139 and lastState terminated exitCode 139 reason Error (restartCount 2 at 06:57:52Z); by 06:59:38Z the container was waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff and restartCount 4, message 'back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=cart'.

Deployment cart in namespace astronomy-shop has replicas=1 but no availableReplicas and no readyReplicas, while all 22 other application Deployments in the namespace show 1 available and 1 ready (namespace also contains grafana).

The cart container logs 'fail: cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore[0]' and 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' at 2026-11-25T06:57:27.93Z and 06:57:38.97Z, with stack frames at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:101) and ValkeyCartStore.Initialize (ValkeyCartStore.cs:71) reached from Program.Main.

The previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-zmjv9 logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 2026-11-25T06:56:30.04Z and continued serving ValkeyCartStore calls (GetCartAsync, AddItemAsync, EmptyCartAsync) until 06:57:23.99Z, then logged 'Application is shutting down...' at 06:57:25.89Z; kubelet recorded a Normal 'Stopping container cart' event for that pod at 06:57:25Z and the same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created pod cart-74587775fc-f2gwb at 06:57:25Z.

The valkey-cart server reports errorstat_NOAUTH count=1626 and total_error_replies=1628 at 06:58:25Z, rising to errorstat_NOAUTH count=2096 and total_error_replies=2098 at 06:59:38Z, i.e. it is answering unauthenticated client commands with NOAUTH continuously during the incident.

The valkey-cart server configuration contains a requirepass parameter (value redacted, so not verifiable) and its INFO server section shows config_file empty; Deployment valkey-cart (generation 1, created 06:56:24Z by helm) declares no command, no args, no env and no volumes, and its only writes are the helm Apply at 2026-11-25T06:56:24Z and a controller status update at 06:56:28Z - so no authentication setting is declared in the workload object.

Deployment cart declares VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and no Redis/Valkey password or username variable; its pod template is unchanged (generation 1, helm Apply 2026-11-25T06:56:24Z) and no NetworkPolicy exists anywhere in the cluster, so nothing at the pod-network level blocks cart->valkey-cart.

valkey-cart pod valkey-cart-859985f49d-nv6sx is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, and the valkey-cart Endpoints object has a ready address 10.244.234.134:6379 on node sregym-worker; in contrast the cart Endpoints object has only notReadyAddresses (10.244.125.5:8080, pod cart-74587775fc-f2gwb).

checkout emitted its own error spans at 06:57:43-06:57:44Z: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and description 'connection error: ... dial tcp 10.96.101.179:8080: connect: connection refused', and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and otel.status_description 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'.

frontend emitted its own HTTP 500 error spans on POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout between 06:57:37Z and 06:57:44Z with exception messages '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.101.179:8080' and '13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'; the same traces contain error spans (http.status_code 500) on frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress'/'POST' and on load-generator 'POST'.

Apart from cart, all 27 other pods in namespace astronomy-shop observed at 06:57:49Z were Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (cart-74587775fc-f2gwb was the only pod with restarts, 1 at that moment, and ready=false).

Most likely cause: the valkey-cart server now requires client authentication (requirepass / password-protected default user) while the cart service connects with VALKEY_ADDR only and no credentials, so every fresh cart connection is answered with NOAUTH and the cart container aborts at startup ('Wasn't able to connect to redis'), producing the CrashLoopBackOff and the cart outage. The cart pod that ran before 06:57:25 authenticated successfully with the same unchanged pod template, so the auth requirement must have been applied to the already-running valkey-cart process at some point between 06:56:30Z and 06:57:27Z rather than declared in any workload spec.

valkey-cart itself is not crashed, restarted or resource-starved: its pod is Ready with restartCount 0, uptime matched pod start (uptime_in_seconds 120 at 06:58:25Z), used_memory 1.31M with maxmemory 0, evicted_keys 0, rejected_connections 0 and connected_clients 2, so the failure is an authentication refusal, not a dead or overloaded dependency.

A pod deletion/rollout of cart is not by itself the fault: the replacement was created by the same ReplicaSet (cart-74587775fc) with an unchanged pod template (Deployment cart generation 1, no spec writes after the 06:56:24Z helm Apply), and the new pod fails with its own application exception, so the restart merely exposed the fault rather than caused it.

Network blocking, DNS or missing endpoints are not the cause of cart's Redis failure: no NetworkPolicy exists in the cluster, the cart init container resolved and opened valkey-cart (10.96.78.71:6379) at 06:57:26Z, the valkey-cart Endpoints object has a ready address, and the server answers cart's commands with NOAUTH (a protocol-level reply, not a connection refusal).

The transient ECONNREFUSED errors frontend logged at 06:56:50-06:57:03Z towards product-catalog (10.96.4.197:8080) and flagd (10.96.137.224:8013) were considered as a competing cause but are startup races of the freshly deployed pods (all pods started 06:56:24-06:57:25Z, product-catalog and flagd Deployments report 1 available/1 ready) and are not tied to the cart failure that began at 06:57:27Z.

Restore a consistent Redis credential configuration between cart and valkey-cart: either clear the authentication requirement on the valkey-cart server (the setting is not declared in its Deployment spec, so it was changed on the running process) or add the matching password/ACL credentials to the cart Deployment and restart cart, then verify that a fresh cart pod logs 'Successfully connected to Redis' and that errorstat_NOAUTH stops increasing.

gaps: The requirepass/ACL value on valkey-cart is redacted by the read-only Redis interface, so the credential itself could not be verified; only the effect (NOAUTH replies) is observed.

The exact time the valkey-cart authentication requirement was applied is unknown (it was not in effect when the previous cart pod connected at 06:56:30Z and was in effect by 06:57:27Z); the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The actor/object that stopped pod cart-74587775fc-zmjv9 at 06:57:25Z is unknown: only a kubelet Normal 'Stopping container cart' event exists, with no controller delete event and no Deployment scale-down event.

Prometheus traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned 0 rate/increase for every service and span name at 06:57:46Z despite traffic being visible in Jaeger and Loki, so metric-based error rates and latency baselines could not be used and no latency trend is claimed.
Container logs timestamped after the authorized window end 06:57:46Z (including the later cart crash attempts) could not be read; the post-window state comes only from cluster object state.
Checkout produced no application log lines matching error/cart in 06:56:30-06:57:46Z, so its impact is evidenced only by its own error spans, not by its logs.
next_steps: Inspect how the valkey-cart server's requirepass/ACL was changed (kubectl exec history, audit logs, or the injector's own records) since no workload object declares it.
Compare the deployed cart/valkey-cart manifests with the upstream OpenTelemetry Demo 2.2.0 chart to confirm whether the password requirement is a deliberate local override or a drift.

After fixing credentials, confirm recovery by watching cart Deployment availableReplicas, the cart Endpoints ready address, cart logs 'Successfully connected to Redis', and a flattening errorstat_NOAUTH on valkey-cart.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
